# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2025-01-22-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (39,427 frames, 26 MB, capture window 2025-01-22 23:44:56 UTC to 2025-01-23 00:38:18 UTC, ~53 min)
- No separate IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence folder; all findings below are derived directly from packet/flow analysis with `tshark`.

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** | DHCP, all traffic |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** | Ethernet header, DHCP client-id |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (domain `bluemoontuesday.com`) | DHCP option 12/81, NBNS, DNS |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS CNameString between 10.1.17.215 and DC 10.1.17.2 (10.1.17.2 = `BLUEMOONTUESDAY` DC, MAC `00:24:e8:7f:09:5d`) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Behavioral classification only — not signature-confirmed.** No Suricata/IDS alert file accompanied the pcap, so there is no rule-hit to cite. Based on TTPs observed in traffic, this is a **"ClickFix"-style fake-CAPTCHA loader that deploys an abused/repackaged TeamViewer client for hands-on-keyboard remote access** (commonly referred to in incident-response writeups as a "ClickFix + TeamViewer hidden-remote-access RAT"). No AV/YARA/signature engine was run against the extracted payloads in this exercise, so the family name is a behavioral assessment, not a confirmed detection.

Chain of behavior observed:
1. **Lure/delivery (ClickFix pattern):** victim browses `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` (fake Google Authenticator verification page) → `authenticatoor.org` → `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (redirect/staging chain), consistent with a fake "verify you are human" page that tricks the user into pasting a command into the Windows Run dialog.
2. **Initial execution:** `mshta.exe` (identified by its default User-Agent `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; ...Trident/7.0...)`) fetches a VBScript component (`get-file/264872`) that opens a decoy browser tab (`azure.microsoft.com`) while silently launching hidden PowerShell.
3. **Loader/beacon:** PowerShell downloads and executes `get-file/29842.ps1`, which reads the C: volume serial number, converts it to decimal, and uses it as a per-host bot ID. It then loops forever: `GET http://5.252.153.241/<serial-id>` every 5 seconds, `Invoke-Expression`-ing whatever is returned (an open-ended remote-command backdoor). This beacon (`/1517096937`) runs for the remainder of the capture.
4. **Second-stage payload push:** the C2 pushes commands that download `TeamViewer` (full GUI executable), `TV` (a DLL), and `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (a DLL) — i.e., attacker silently stages a TeamViewer install for covert remote control.
5. **Persistence:** malware reports back `message = startup shortcut created; status = success` — confirms a Startup-folder shortcut was created for auto-run at logon.
6. **Remote-control channel:** TeamViewer components then register with the legitimate TeamViewer master server (`master16.teamviewer.com`) via the DynGate protocol, and a large, sustained (~28.6-minute) TLS session with a **self-signed certificate** opens directly to a bare IP over a non-standard port — consistent with attacker hands-on-keyboard access.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### C2 / malicious network endpoints
| IP:Port | Role |
|---|---|
| **5.252.153.241:80** | Primary loader/C2 — plaintext HTTP, hosts `/api/file/get-file/*` payload API and the `/<disk-serial>` command-polling beacon |
| **45.125.66.32:2917** | Post-compromise remote-control/C2 channel — TLS with self-signed cert, no SNI/domain, direct-IP, ~10.3 MB over ~28.6 min (largest single conversation in the capture) |
| **45.125.66.252:443** | Secondary channel in the same /24 as above, same session window |
| **82.221.136.26:443** | `authenticatoor.org` — ClickFix lure page |
| **104.21.64.1:443** (Cloudflare-fronted) | `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` — fake Google Authenticator lure page |
| **217.70.186.109:443** | `appointedtimeagriculture.com` — redirector/staging domain in the lure chain |
| **185.188.32.26:80** | `master16.teamviewer.com` — legitimate TeamViewer master server, abused via DynGate protocol (`din.aspx`/`dout.aspx`) as rendezvous for the attacker-controlled TeamViewer session |

### Malicious domains
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net`
- `authenticatoor.org`
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com`

### Malicious URLs (host 5.252.153.241)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (VBScript/HTA scriptlet loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` (PowerShell beacon loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` (duplicate beacon loader, re-served)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/1517096937` (repeating C2 beacon/poll, disk-serial-derived bot ID; also seen with `?k=` status callbacks, e.g. `message = startup shortcut created; status = success`)

### Transferred files and SHA256 hashes (extracted from HTTP objects in this pcap)
| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| `264872` (VBScript/HTA component, `application/octet-stream`) | `c74123dbccded43fda61651e102750b041d4c3af6fda88cd6436f9276653e103` — *(65-char string, see note)* |
| `29842.ps1` (PowerShell beacon loader) | `b8ce40900788ea26b9e4c9af7efab533e8d39ed1370da09b93fcf72a16750ded` — *(same note)* |
| `pas.ps1` (identical beacon loader, re-served) | `a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e` |
| `TeamViewer` (PE32 GUI executable) | `904280f20d697d876ab90a1b74c0f22a83b859e8b0519cb411fda26f1642f53e` |
| `Teamviewer_Resource_fr` (PE32 DLL) | `9634ecaf469149379bba80a745f53d823948c41ce4e347860701cbdff6935192` |
| `TV` (PE32 DLL) | `3448da03808f24568e6181011f8521c0713ea6160efd05bff20c43b091ff59f7` |

*(Note: verified with `shasum -a 256` these are standard 64-hex-char SHA256 digests; recheck formatting if copy/pasting — no extra characters were actually appended, an earlier terminal rendering artifact made two of them look one character longer.)*

## Recommended Actions
1. Isolate **10.1.17.215 (DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ)** from the network immediately.
2. Reset credentials for **shutchenson** (domain account) and check the DC (`10.1.17.2`) for any lateral Kerberos/LDAP activity from this session.
3. Block outbound to `5.252.153.241`, `45.125.66.32`, `45.125.66.252`, `82.221.136.26`, `104.21.64.1` (host header only), `217.70.186.109`, and the three malicious domains at the perimeter/DNS layer.
4. Hunt for the Startup-folder shortcut and the staged `TeamViewer`/`TV`/`Teamviewer_Resource_fr` files on disk; treat any TeamViewer install on this host as attacker-controlled, not legitimate IT tooling.
5. Since attribution here is behavioral only, submit the extracted files (hashes above) to an AV/sandbox engine before closing out family attribution.
